name: Ish-bosheth
description: Saul's son living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul and made him king over Gilead and Israel; Ishbosheth was forty years old and reigned two years, while Judah followed David. David reigned in Hebron over Judah seven years and six months.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul. When Ishbosheth charged him over Rizpah, Saul's concubine, Abner was very wroth, saying he had shown kindness to the house of Saul and not delivered them to David, and now was charged with a fault concerning this woman.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner sent messengers to David offering to bring all Israel to him. David agreed to make a league, but required that Michal, Saul's daughter, first be brought to him, and he sent to Ishbosheth to deliver his wife whom he had espoused for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: The sons of Rimmon came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon in the hottest part of the day, and came into the midst of the house as though they would fetch wheat, and smote him under the fifth rib.

Rechab and Baanah escaped, having smitten and slain him on his bed; and they beheaded him and took his head and got away through the plain all night, and brought the head to David at Hebron, saying, Behold the head of Ishbosheth thine enemy, and claiming the Lord had avenged the king this day of Saul and his seed.

David commanded his young men, and they slew Rechab and Baanah, cut off their hands and feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron, but took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner. The Most High has His own way of doing things; His people are not to put the cart before the horse.
